title: Assad means happy
body:
Assad is 24 years old, from Syria. He comes from a family with 9 other siblings.
He is married and has a one-year-old child. Due to the civil war happening in his country, he saw one of his brothers forced to kill another brother of his.
"I didn't want to kill anyone" and in 2015 (at 15 years old) he left for Istanbul.
"I couldn't find work in Turkey, there is a lot of racism. I couldn't feed my family" and, last October, he got on a boat in the Sea of Marmara and crossed over to the island of Leros (illegally, he said), for €6,000. His wife and child stayed behind.
Since February he has been working in Athens, at a textile factory.
He hasn't seen his parents and siblings for 10 years.
-Is Syria beautiful, Assad?
-Very. Until they destroyed it.
For 4 hours we were sitting next to each other on the train and hadn't exchanged a word. Until, with immense politeness and a smile, he asked me "Athens?" pointing at his watch. I told him in English "we are arriving now in an hour." He didn't understand. Because he didn't know a single word of English. And for the remaining hour we had a unique conversation through sign language and Google Translate. Him in Arabic, me in Greek.
Assad wasn't educated, he left school so he wouldn't die. And yet he is a dignified man, smiling.
However
Assad is not happy or content.
-It was my honor to meet you. You are good.
-The honor is mine, Assad.

y.f.
